name: John Ford
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: John Ford (baptised 1586 in Devon, died about 1639) trained at the Middle Temple and wrote for the Caroline stage, both alone and with Thomas Dekker and William Rowley. His best-known plays are 'Tis Pity She's a Whore, The Broken Heart and Perkin Warbeck.

The two songs here, from The Lover's Melancholy (1629) and The Broken Heart (1633), are the ones printed under his name in A. H. Bullen's Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age (1889). Songs from The Sun's Darling, which he wrote with Dekker, are filed under Dekker.

poems.title: Fly Hence, Shadows!
poems.author: John Ford
poems.collection: Lyrics from the Dramatists of the Elizabethan Age, ed. A. H. Bullen (London: Nimmo, 1889)
poems.text:
Fly hence, shadows, that do keep
Watchful sorrows charmed in sleep!

Tho' the eyes be overtaken,
Yet the heart doth ever waken
Thoughts, chained up in busy snares
Of continual woes and cares:
Love and griefs are so exprest
As they rather sigh than rest.

Fly hence, shadows, that do keep
Watchful sorrows charmed in sleep!
